column1: The history of human civilisation is entwined with the history of the ways we have learned to manipulate water resources.
column2: 人类文明的历史，与我们利用水资源的方式密切相关。

column1: As towns gradually expanded, water was brought from increasingly remote sources, leading to sophisticated engineering efforts such as dams and aqueducts.
column2: 随着城镇逐渐扩张，水被从越来越遥远的源头引来，促使人们修建了诸如水坝和输水渠等复杂工程。

column1: At the height of the Roman Empire, nine major systems, with an innovative layout of pipes and well-built sewers, supplied the occupants of Rome with as much water per person as is provided in many parts of the industrial world today.
column2: 在罗马帝国的鼎盛时期，九套大型供水系统采用新颖的管网布局，配有坚固的下水道，罗马居民的人均供水量可与今天许多工业化地区相当。
column3: At the height of|在……的鼎盛时期

column1: During the industrial revolution and population explosion of the 19th and 20th centuries, the demand for water rose dramatically.
column2: 在19世纪和20世纪工业革命及人口激增期间，对水的需求急剧增长。

column1: Unprecedented construction of tens of thousands of monumental engineering projects designed to control floods, protect clean water supplies, and provide water for irrigation and hydropower brought great benefits to hundreds of millions of people.
column2: 当时兴建了数以万计的大型工程，规模空前。这些工程旨在防洪、保障清洁水供应，并为灌溉和水力发电供水，给数亿人带来了巨大的好处。
column5: tens of thousands of|数以万计的
column15: brought great benefits to|给……带来巨大好处
column16: hundreds of millions of|数以亿计的

column1: Food production has kept pace with soaring populations mainly because of the expansion of artificial irrigation systems that make possible the growth of 40 % of the world’s food.
column2: 粮食生产一直赶得上人口的急速增长，主要得益于人工灌溉系统的扩展。正是这些系统使全球40%的粮食得以种植。
column8: artificial irrigation systems|人工灌溉系统

column1: Nearly one fifth of all the electricity generated worldwide is produced by turbines spun by the power of falling water.
column2: 全球范围内，约有五分之一的电力是通过利用落水的力量来驱动涡轮机产生的。

column1: Yet there is a dark side to this picture: despite our progress, half of the world’s population still suffers, with water services inferior to those available to the ancient Greeks and Romans.
column2: 然而，这幅图景也有阴暗的一面：尽管我们取得了进步，世界上仍有一半人口深受供水条件差之苦，他们享有的供水服务甚至比不上古希腊人和古罗马人。

column1: As the United Nations report on access to water reiterated in November 2001, more than one billion people lack access to clean drinking water; some two and a half billion do not have adequate sanitation services.
column2: 正如联合国在2001年11月发布的关于水资源获取情况的报告中所指出的，有超过十亿人无法获得清洁饮用水；而约二十亿人口则缺乏足够的卫生设施。

column1: Preventable water-related diseases kill an estimated 10,000 to 20,000 children every day, and the latest evidence suggests that we are falling behind in efforts to solve these problems.
column2: 据估计，与水有关的可预防疾病每天夺去一万至两万名儿童的生命。最新证据表明，我们解决这些问题的步伐正在落后。

column1: The consequences of our water policies extend beyond jeopardising human health.
column2: 我们的用水政策带来的后果，除了危及人类健康，还涉及其他方面。

column1: Tens of millions of people have been forced to move from their homes - often with little warning or compensation - to make way for the reservoirs behind dams.
column2: 数以千万计的人被迫离开自己的家园——通常是在没有任何预兆或补偿的情况下——为修建水库而迁移。

column1: More than 20% of all freshwater fish species are now threatened or endangered because dams and water withdrawals have destroyed the free-flowing river ecosystems where they thrive.
column2: 目前，超过20%的淡水鱼类物种面临生存威胁或濒临灭绝，因为水坝建设和水资源过度抽取已破坏了它们赖以生存的自由流动河流生态系统。

column1: Certain irrigation practices degrade soil quality and reduce agricultural productivity.
column2: 某些灌溉方式会使土壤质量下降，降低农业生产率。

column1: Groundwater aquifers are being pumped down faster than they are naturally replenished in parts of India, China, the USA and elsewhere.
column2: 在印度、中国、美国及世界其他一些地区，地下水蓄水层的抽水速度已超过其自然补给速度。

column1: And disputes over shared water resources have led to violence and continue to raise local, national and even international tensions.
column2: 关于共享水资源的争议已引发暴力，并持续加剧着地方、国家乃至国际层面的紧张局势。

column1: At the outset of the new millennium, however, the way resource planners think about water is beginning to change.
column2: 然而，在新千年的开始之际，资源规划者们对水资源管理的思维方式正在发生变革。

column1: The focus is slowly shifting back to the provision of basic human and environmental needs as top priority – ensuring ‘some for all,’ instead of ‘more for some’.
column2: 重心正慢慢回到这样一个首要任务上：满足人类和环境的基本用水需求，确保“人人都能分到一些”，而不是“让少数人得到更多”。
column7: human and environmental needs|人类和环境的需求
column12: more for some|少数人得到更多

column1: Some water experts are now demanding that existing infrastructure be used in smarter ways rather than building new facilities, which is increasingly considered the option of last, not first, resort.
column2: 如今，一些水务专家要求更巧妙地利用现有的基础设施，而不是新建设施。越来越多的人认为，新建设施应是最后才考虑的办法，而不应是首选。

column1: This shift in philosophy has not been universally accepted, and it comes with strong opposition from some established water organisations.
column2: 这种哲学观念的转变并未得到普遍认可，一些权威的水资源保护组织对此提出了强烈反对。

column1: Nevertheless, it may be the only way to address successfully the pressing problems of providing everyone with clean water to drink, adequate water to grow food and a life free from preventable water-related illness.
column2: 尽管如此，这也许是解决下列紧迫问题的唯一办法：让人人都有干净的水喝，有足够的水种粮食，生活中免受那些本可预防的涉水疾病之苦。

column1: Fortunately - and unexpectedly - the demand for water is not rising as rapidly as some predicted.
column2: 幸运的是——出乎意料的是——对水的需求并没有像一些人预测的那样迅速上升。

column1: As a result, the pressure to build new water infrastructures has diminished over the past two decades.
column2: 因此，在过去二十年里，建设新的水利基础设施的压力已经有所减轻。

column1: Although population, industrial output and economic productivity have continued to soar in developed nations, the rate at which people withdraw water from aquifers, rivers and lakes has slowed.
column2: 虽然发达国家的人口、工业产值和经济生产力持续上升，但人们从含水层、河流和湖泊中抽取水资源的速度却有所减缓。

column1: And in a few parts of the world, demand has actually fallen.
column2: 在世界某些地区，需求实际上已下降。

column1: What explains this remarkable turn of events?
column2: 是什么导致了这一显著的变化呢？

column1: Two factors: people have figured out how to use water more efficiently, and communities are rethinking their priorities for water use.
column2: 有两个因素：人们已经掌握了更高效地利用水资源的方法；各个社区正在重新思考自己在水资源利用方面的优先事项。

column1: Throughout the first three-quarters of the 20th century, the quantity of freshwater consumed per person doubled on average; in the USA, water withdrawals increased tenfold while the population quadrupled.
column2: 在20世纪的头75年里，人均淡水用量平均翻了一番。在美国，取水量增至原来的十倍，而人口增至原来的四倍。
column4: first three-quarters|n. 最初的四分之三

column1: But since 1980, the amount of water consumed per person has actually decreased, thanks to a range of new technologies that help to conserve water in homes and industry.
column2: 但自1980年以来，人均用水量实际上已减少，这得益于一系列新技术在家庭和工业领域中的节水作用。

column1: In 1965, for instance, Japan used approximately 13 million gallons of water to produce $1 million of commercial output; by 1989 this had dropped to 3.5 million gallons (even accounting for inflation) - almost a quadrupling of water productivity.
column2: 例如，1965年，日本每创造100万美元的商业产值，大约需要1300万加仑水。到1989年，即使计入通货膨胀，每创造同样的产值也只需350万加仑水，相当于每加仑水能创造的产值几乎增至原来的四倍。
column12: water productivity|单位用水量创造的产值

column1: In the USA, water withdrawals have fallen by more than 20 % from their peak in 1980.
column2: 在美国，水的提取量比1980年的峰值减少了20%以上。

column1: On the other hand, dams, aqueducts and other kinds of infrastructure will still have to be built, particularly in developing countries where basic human needs have not been met.
column2: 另一方面，仍然需要建设水坝、渠道等各种基础设施，尤其是在那些基本需求尚未得到满足的发展中国家。
column3: On the other hand|另一方面

column1: But such projects must be built to higher specifications and with more accountability to local people and their environment than in the past.
column2: 但与过去相比，这类工程必须按更高的标准建设，也须对当地居民及其生活环境承担更多责任。

column1: And even in regions where new projects seem warranted, we must find ways to meet demands with fewer resources, respecting ecological criteria and to a smaller budget.
column2: 即使有些地区看来确有必要新建工程，我们也必须设法用更少的资源满足需求，遵守生态标准，并把开支控制在更低的预算内。
